title: Python String Escape Characters
learningObjectives: Explain the core rules of python string escape characters in Python.

understand.concept: An escape sequence begins with a backslash inside a string literal and represents a character that is difficult to type directly or has special meaning. Common sequences include newline, tab, backslash and quote escapes. Raw string literals change how backslashes are interpreted, with important delimiter rules.
understand.whyItMatters: Escape sequences allow programs to represent line breaks, tabs, quotation marks and paths accurately without confusing the Python parser.
understand.analogy: An escape sequence is like a notation mark in a script that tells the reader to interpret the next symbol in a special way.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is limited because escape processing is defined by Python's lexical rules and differs between ordinary, raw and bytes literals.

explain.narrative:
## Common escape sequences
Inside an ordinary string literal, `\\n` represents a newline, `\\t` a tab, `\\\\` a literal backslash, and `\\'` or `\\"` an escaped quote. These sequences are interpreted when Python parses the literal.

## Raw strings
A raw string such as `r'C:\\work\\notes'` keeps backslashes as ordinary characters for most escape sequences. Raw strings are useful for regular-expression patterns and Windows-style paths. A raw string cannot end with an odd number of backslashes because the final backslash would escape the closing quote at the lexical level.

## Display and debugging
`print()` displays actual newline and tab characters. `repr()` shows an escaped representation useful for debugging. Do not confuse the two displays: they describe the same string in different ways.

examples.title: Insert a newline
examples.explanation: The escape sequence \\n represents a line-feed character, so print displays a new line.

examples.title: Insert a tab
examples.explanation: The \\t escape represents a horizontal tab.

examples.title: Include quotation marks
examples.explanation: Escaping the inner single quotes prevents them from terminating the literal.

examples.title: Represent a backslash
examples.explanation: In an ordinary literal, each backslash is written as \\\\ to represent one literal backslash.

examples.title: Use a raw path string
examples.explanation: The raw-string prefix preserves backslashes instead of interpreting sequences such as \\t.

questions.prompt: Which escape sequence represents a newline?
questions.explanation: Backslash-n is the newline escape sequence in an ordinary string literal.

questions.prompt: Which escape sequence represents a tab?

questions.answer: An escaped representation useful for inspecting characters
options: An escaped representation useful for inspecting characters
Only the visible text without quotes
questions.explanation: repr returns a representation that makes escapes and otherwise non-obvious characters easier to inspect.

questions.prompt: What is a common restriction on raw string literals?
questions.answer: They cannot end with an odd number of backslashes
options: They cannot end with an odd number of backslashes
questions.explanation: A final unpaired backslash would escape the closing quote in the source literal.

questions.prompt: What does print('A\\nB') display when the source contains backslash-n?
questions.answer: A and B on separate lines
options: A and B on separate lines
The two characters backslash and n between A and B
questions.explanation: In an ordinary literal, \\n is interpreted as a newline before print writes the string.
